findings.reason: The protected Python solution determines if a person can attend all meetings by sorting the interval list by start time and checking for any overlapping adjacent intervals. It returns False if any interval starts before the previous interval ends. The solution runs in O(n log n) time and O(n) space for Timsort; no candidate is required.

Sorting intervals by start time guarantees that any potential overlap must occur between adjacent intervals, making a single linear scan of consecutive pairs necessary and sufficient to detect conflicts.
Sorting n intervals takes O(n log n) time, followed by an O(n) linear scan to verify non-overlapping boundaries. Auxiliary space is O(n) for Timsort. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts list of intervals [start, end], returning a boolean indicating if all meetings can be attended without overlap.

The approach accurately details start-time sorting, adjacent interval overlap checking, and O(n log n) time / O(n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover all-pairs quadratic comparisons, empty/singleton interval lists, and touching endpoint non-overlap rules.
